title: The Corn at Night
subtitle: Monday 7 to Thursday 10 October 1974: An Old Woman's Kitchen, a Line of Flashlights, Something in the Rows and the Water

setting.name: The stone house, the Fossum corn and the north branch of Hollow Fork Creek, 7 to 10 October 1974
setting.description: Five days to Harvest Days, and the town has closed. After the party's visit to the hired man's house, Arnie Fossum and the board moved Dawn on Monday 7 October to the one house in Hollow Fork they trust absolutely: Ingeborg Vaage's stone house on the rim of the Hollow. They were wrong to trust it. Ingeborg sends for the party and tells them everything she has kept for seventy years, and offers them the one night she can give them: Wednesday 9 October, when she will tell Arnie on channel 14 that the girl is asleep. Between the stone house and running water lie the windbreak, the rim path and four hundred acres of the Fossums' standing corn, nine feet tall, dry and rustling, with a grass waterway down the middle and the north branch of Hollow Fork Creek along the far edge, three-quarters of a mile away. On Tuesday the Fork bridge is closed 'for repairs' with two grain trucks parked across it and County Road K over the ridge is closed 'for a washout'; on Wednesday night, because the town is not stupid, Arnie Fossum's line walks the corn: twenty-four men with flashlights, red kerchiefs wetted over their mouths, CB walkie-talkies on channel 14, two tractors with their headlights on, the Fossum dogs. And in the rows, because its guest is leaving its land, something else walks too. It cannot take Dawn before Harvest Days. It can hold her for the men to find. On Thursday the telephone exchange goes down, and Harald Haugen, at his desk, has to decide what to write.
setting.atmosphere: Night, corn and cold. The corn at night is a world of its own: walls of dry stalks taller than a man on every side, leaves like paper knives that whisper and rasp at the slightest touch, a strip of stars overhead, the ground soft and uneven, rows that all look the same. Flashlight beams flicker through the stalks like lightning in a cloud. The CB walkie-talkies crackle with farm voices trying to sound calm. Tractor headlights sweep. The dogs bay. And then, in a part of the field where nobody is, the rustling stops, and the stalks go white with frost in a moving line, and something breathes in. This is the campaign's pursuit-and-hiding night: run it as a series of short tense legs, let the players hide, run, split and be brave, and let the rules they have learned save them.

keyLocations.name: Ingeborg Vaage's Stone House
keyLocations.description: The fieldstone house on the rim, lilacs, a slate roof, a kitchen with a wood range and a table covered in oilcloth, a parlour full of photographs, a narrow stair, and a hand pump at the back step running into a stone trough and overflowing into a ditch that runs across the yard and down over the rim, all day and all night. Dawn is in the little bedroom at the top of the stair. Ingeborg has stopped giving her Dr. Kubicek's tonic and the town's bread; she has been feeding her on oatmeal from a box Rolf brought from Linden Falls. Dawn is clearer every hour, and more frightened.
features: The running pump and the ditch across the yard: a wall
Ingeborg's CB on the kitchen dresser, tuned to 14
The parlour photographs: her father Halvor and her mother, 1904; her wedding, 1915; seventy Harvest Days
encounters: Rolf Haugen, who has been bringing groceries
secrets: CLUE 4d (core): Ingeborg was there. She was twelve, and she followed her father down the rim path on the night of 24 August 1904 and hid behind the Union Church and watched the seven men go down to the Cold Hole with lanterns, and heard the cold speak to them in her mother's voice, and heard the terms, and heard her father say yes. She confirms all four rules, and the two doors, in the words she heard. 'It said, the lease runs until every house that set its name to it unsays it here, or until the hand that writes my guests' names comes down to me in their stead. My father thought that was a kindness. A door out. He never used it.'

CLUE 3d (core, if not already given): 'It can't see, child. It listens for your breath. Wet your kerchief in running water and pull it up. Lie down with your face in the dirt. Hold your breath when it's close. Don't carry a light if you don't have to; it likes warmth, and light is warm.'
Ingeborg will speak for the house of Vaage at the Cold Hole, first, if anyone asks her. 'I've been waiting seventy years for someone to ask me.'

keyLocations.name: The Fossum Corn
keyLocations.description: Four hundred acres of field corn, planted in thirty-inch rows running north and south, nine feet tall, dry-down nearly done, the ears hanging. By custom the Fossums do not pick the rows nearest the Hollow until after Harvest Days. A grass waterway, thirty feet wide, runs down the middle of the field from the rim to the creek bottom: open ground, mown, the fastest route and the most exposed. A township gravel road, Fossum Lane, crosses the field east to west halfway down, with the Fossum yard lights a quarter mile to the west of where it meets the waterway. At the bottom, the land drops into a strip of willows and box elder and the north branch of Hollow Fork Creek, ankle-deep to knee-deep, fast and cold over gravel.
features: Rows: walls of stalks on both sides, a leaf-rasp at every step (Stealth at disadvantage if running)
The waterway: open, mown, starlit, fast (double speed, no cover)
Fossum Lane: gravel, a tractor on it with its headlights on
A tile-drain outlet, a culvert under Fossum Lane, big enough to crawl through (Perception DC 13 to find)
encounters: Arnie Fossum's line: twenty-four men (Frightened Townsman stats; Arnie and three of the bigger men as Night Watchman), in pairs, a pair every fifty yards, sweeping north to south from the yard and east to west along the lane
The Fossum dogs, two (Feral Dog stats), loose in the field with the line
The Landlord in the rows (campaign controlFile)
Shades of the guests, calling (Shade stats; they do not attack unless followed; they are a lure and a terror)
secrets: The line's plan, for anyone listening on channel 14 (Ward's scanner, Ingeborg's set, a walkie-talkie lifted from a townsman): pairs every fifty yards, sweeping south from the yard at ten-thirty; the tractor on Fossum Lane; two men at the bridge; two at the creek where the waterway meets it. Hearing the plan gives advantage on the first leg.

The Landlord comes up the waterway from the Hollow at about eleven, and goes wherever there is the most breath: the line, because twenty-four men breathing hard in kerchiefs are still breathing, frightens it away from them less than the party might hope; it moves through the field like a slow white wind, frosting the stalks in a line twenty feet wide.

The townsmen are as frightened of it as the party is. When it comes through, they lie down in the rows with their faces in the dirt and their wet kerchiefs over their mouths, every one, and the line stops. That is the party's chance.

keyLocations.name: The North Branch and the Fork Bridge
keyLocations.description: The north branch of Hollow Fork Creek, twelve feet wide, fast and cold over gravel, knee-deep at most, with willows and box elder along both banks, and the far bank outside the Landlord's land. A mile downstream, at the edge of the village, the Fork bridge, a 1931 concrete span, closed since Tuesday with two co-op grain trucks parked nose to nose across it and a sawhorse reading BRIDGE CLOSED — CO-OP REPAIRS. Beyond it, County Road K's west leg to La Crosse.
features: The creek: running water, the wall; once across, the Landlord cannot follow and the town's men will not cross on foot at night
The bridge: two grain trucks, two men in a pickup, a CB
encounters: Two men at the creek where the waterway meets it (Frightened Townsman stats), with flashlights
Two men at the bridge in a pickup; Arnie can bring the Fossums' combine across the bridge road in four minutes
secrets: Once Dawn is across running water and outside the watershed, the Landlord cannot touch her, ever, while she stays out (Rule Two). The town knows it. They will stop chasing at the creek, and stand on the bank with their flashlights, and some of them will cry.

The bridge can be forced: Ward Mrozek's Kenworth (or any heavy truck) against the two grain trucks, Driving DC 15, an eighteen-wheeler's weight shoving them aside in a scream of metal; or Rolf Haugen can simply drive one of the co-op trucks off the bridge, since he has the keys. Either is a set piece; either commits the party to open war with the town.

keyLocations.name: The Telephone Exchange
keyLocations.description: A brick hut behind the village hall, the Hollow Fork Telephone Cooperative's dial exchange: racks of relays, a battery room, a test board, and a cable that runs out under Main Street. On Thursday 10 October at seven in the morning, Arnie Fossum's oldest son pulls the main fuses, and every telephone in Hollow Fork goes dead, and the town tells anyone who asks that it's the storm damage. There was no storm.
features: The fuse panel and a padlock
The test board, from which a Mechanics character can make one call out over the long-distance trunk (Mechanics DC 14) once the fuses are back
encounters: Nobody, except at shift change, when a Fossum boy looks in
secrets: With the phones down, the party's only contact with the outside is CB (Ward's rig reaches truckers on the interstate on channel 19 at night with Mechanics DC 12 for the antenna), Deputy Garnett's cruiser radio, Emil Pospisil's Friday bus, and the TV van coming on Saturday.

keyLocations.name: Harald Haugen's Office, Thursday Night
keyLocations.description: The co-op office after midnight on Thursday 10 October: one desk lamp, the green safe standing open, the Book on the blotter, a fountain pen, Harald in his shirtsleeves. If Dawn got out of the watershed, he has struck her name through with one line in the presence of the board at six o'clock that evening, and inked the alternate's name under it, because the board told him to and because the Book says the rent must be paid. If Dawn did not get out, she is in Dr. Kubicek's clinic, sedated, and Harald has written nothing new.
features: The Book, open at the 1974 line
A bottle of rye he has not opened
A photograph of his late wife Anna and Rolf at sixteen
secrets: Harald will come to the party, or let them in (core, if they have Rolf with them, or the Book, or the stones; Persuasion DC 15 otherwise): he is done. He tells them he struck the girl's name and wrote their friend's, and was sick in the washroom afterward. He shows them the first page. He tells them the two doors. He says the surrender is the right one, and that he does not believe the six houses will do it, because he would not have, last year. And he says, very quietly: 'If they won't, there's the other door. It's my hand. It's always been my hand.' GM: this is the seed of the paying out (campaign controlFile outcomes). Do not let a player push him toward it. He has thought about it for nineteen years.

synopsis: Ingeborg Vaage, given Dawn to keep by a town that trusts her, sends for the party instead, and in her kitchen tells them all of it: what she saw at the Cold Hole as a girl of twelve in 1904, the terms in the thing's own words, how to hide from it, and that she will speak first if anyone ever tries to surrender the lease. She offers them Wednesday night. The town closes Hollow Fork on Tuesday: the Fork bridge blocked with grain trucks, the ridge road closed, and on Thursday the phones. On Wednesday night the party takes Dawn out of the stone house and through the Fossum corn toward the north branch of the creek, three-quarters of a mile of standing corn, while Arnie Fossum's line of twenty-four men with flashlights and CB walkie-talkies sweeps the rows, and something else comes up out of the Hollow and walks the field, frosting the stalks, hunting by breath, trying to hold its guest for the men to find. The guests it has taken call names from the rows. The light goes out. If the party reaches running water with Dawn, she is out of its land and safe for good; if not, she is taken back and kept at Dr. Kubicek's clinic. Either way, on Thursday the phones go dead, and that night Harald Haugen, who has struck Dawn's name and inked a player character's under it (or has not yet had to), comes to the party with the Book and tells them he is finished, that the surrender is the right door, and that if the houses will not walk through it there is another door, and it is his.
hook: Monday 7 October, early. Five days to Harvest Days. The town is Watchful or Closed. Rolf Haugen, or Pastor Tove Hagstrom, or a note under the motel door in an old woman's spidery hand: 'They have brought the girl to me. Come to the house after dark. Wet your kerchiefs. I. V.'

conclusions.conclusion: How to hide from it in the corn: hide your breath; it cannot see
clues: 3d: Ingeborg Vaage: 'It listens for your breath' (the stone house)
3b: Kari Brandvold in the furrow, 1904 (Rev. Penrose's register, hs-scenario-002)
3c: the townsmen in the line lying down with their faces in the dirt and wet kerchiefs over their mouths when it comes (the corn)
3a: the frost on the inside of the windows reaching only for breath (hs-scenario-001)

conclusions.conclusion: Running water is the way out: get Dawn over the creek and she is out of its land for good
clues: 2d: Einar Aldahl and the Fork bridge, 1951, and the Book's 'went over the water' (hs-scenario-002)
2a: the frost line of 23 September along the creek bank (hs-scenario-001)
2c: the running pump and the ditch at Ingeborg's step, and every hose in town
The town's men stopping on the creek bank with their flashlights (the corn)

conclusions.conclusion: The two doors out are real, and each has a person who can open it
clues: 4d: Ingeborg, who heard the terms spoken in 1904 and will speak first for the house of Vaage (the stone house)
4a: the Book's first page and its seven house names, shown by Harald (the co-op office)
4b and 4c: Rev. Penrose's register and Einar Aldahl (hs-scenario-002)
Harald Haugen: 'It's my hand. It's always been my hand' (the co-op office, Thursday night)

acts.title: Monday and Tuesday: Closing In
acts.description: The town closes and the party prepares. Ingeborg's kitchen gives them the whole truth and the night they need; channel 14 gives them the town's plan; the party chooses its route and its allies. The point of this act is preparation, so that the night in the corn is the party using what it knows. Let them plan as long as they like, and then let the town close the bridge and the road around them.
objectives: Hear Ingeborg Vaage's account of 1904 and her offer
Learn the town's plan for Wednesday night on channel 14
Choose a route to running water and prepare: kerchiefs, lights, a decoy, a vehicle, allies

scenes.name: Ingeborg's Kitchen
scenes.description: Monday or Tuesday night, the stone house. Ingeborg has coffee, rosettes, and the truth (CLUES 4d and 3d). Dawn comes down the stair in a borrowed housecoat, clear-eyed for the first time in a month, and frightened; with Tess there, she cries for a long time. Ingeborg tells the story of 24 August 1904 from behind the Union Church: the seven men, the lanterns, the cold that spoke in her mother's voice, the terms. Then: 'They brought her to me because I'm a Vaage and I'm old and they think I'm theirs. I've been theirs for seventy years. I'm done. Wednesday night I'll tell Arnie on the radio she's asleep. That's all I can give you. After that you'll have to run.' She will not leave the stone house herself (she is a Vaage, and a Vaage is needed at the Cold Hole). Run this as a long, quiet, frightening scene. It is the campaign's best piece of exposition and it should feel like a confession.
scenes.readAloud: The old woman pours coffee into cups so thin you can see the lamplight through them, and sets a plate of rosettes on the oilcloth, and sits down across from you, and folds her hands. Outside, the pump at the back step runs and runs. "I was twelve," she says. "My mother had the fever. Dr. Holm was dead of it already, and five men, and she was going to be the sixth, and my father sat up with her three nights and on the fourth he went out. I followed him. Down the rim path, in my nightgown and my brother's boots, and I hid behind the church, and I watched seven men go down to the hole with lanterns. Gunnar Haugen. Ole Brandvold. Josef Kubicek. Anders Lunde. Per Fossum. Old Tor Aldahl. My father." She says the names like a list of the dead, which they are. "And the cold came up out of the hole and spoke to them. In my mother's voice. It said what it wanted, and what it would give, and how it could end. And my father said yes, and then they all did." She looks at her hands. "My mother sat up in bed the next morning and asked for coffee. She lived to be ninety. Every year since, I have set a stone."

skillChecks.success: Ingeborg is not asking to be forgiven. She is asking for help, which is harder for her, and she means every word.
skillChecks.failure: An old woman telling a story she has told herself a thousand times.

skillChecks.success: Ingeborg agrees to speak for the house of Vaage at the Cold Hole on Harvest Days, first, before anyone else, and to tell the others she will. 'Let them see an old woman do it. Let them be ashamed.' (Each house the party wins counts in hs-scenario-004.)
skillChecks.failure: Ingeborg says she will speak if the others will. She has never known the others to do anything together but this.

skillChecks.success: Dawn: off the phenobarbital and the bread for two days, pulse steady, pupils normal, frightened and herself. She can walk a mile tonight if someone helps her over rough ground, and she can hold her breath for a round (CON +0). She needs a coat, boots and a kerchief.
skillChecks.failure: Dawn is weak and frightened. You are not sure she can make it a mile through the corn.

scenes.name: Breaker One-Four
scenes.description: Tuesday and Wednesday, channel 14. The town plans in the open, because it is the town's channel and the town does not think anyone else is listening: Arnie (Big Red) organises the line; Vernon and the boys report the bridge and the road closed; somebody's wife is making sandwiches; somebody asks if anyone has told the pastor. Anyone with a CB and a scanner crystal hears the whole plan (see keyLocations: the line's plan). Ward can also go out wider: at night, with Mechanics DC 12 on the rig's antenna, channel 19 reaches the interstate forty miles away, and a trucker called Nightingale will relay a message to the Wisconsin State Patrol, who will tell Sheriff Dahlquist, who will do nothing until Saturday. Deception DC 14 on 14 itself, as a Hollow Fork voice, to feed the line a false report ('they're going down the rim path toward the church!') and pull a section of the line west for one leg.
scenes.readAloud: "Big Red to everybody. Big Red to everybody. Ten-thirty at my yard Wednesday night. Bring your kerchiefs and your good lights. Pairs, fifty yards, like we did for the Lien boy when he got lost. Nobody brings a gun. I mean it. Nobody brings a gun. She's a sick girl and those folks with her are scared and we're not going to hurt anybody." A pause, a crackle. "And if it comes up the field, you know what to do. Same as always. Get down, face down, kerchief up, and wait." Another voice: "Ten-four, Big Red." Another: "Ten-four." Another, a woman: "I'll bring sandwiches to the yard." And then a long silence, and the old flat voice from the elevator, Harald's, very tired: "Ten-four, Arnie. God help us."

skillChecks.success: The scanner crystal and a longer whip: you hear every word on 14 from the motel lot or the stone house, and you can listen on Wednesday night as the line walks, which gives the party advantage on the first leg in the corn.
skillChecks.failure: You catch pieces: Wednesday, ten-thirty, pairs, sandwiches. Enough to know they are coming.

skillChecks.success: Your voice, in a farm accent, at the right moment on Wednesday night, pulls a third of the line west toward the Union Church for one leg. Arnie will know by morning it was you.
skillChecks.failure: Big Red says, 'Who's that? Say your handle,' and you can't, and the channel knows there's a stranger on it.

skillChecks.success: Arnie means it: nobody brings a gun. He is a decent man doing a terrible thing as decently as he can. The men in his line are frightened of the corn at night, and more frightened of what happens to Hollow Fork if the girl gets over the water.
skillChecks.failure: Two dozen men are coming into the corn after you. That is all you hear.

scenes.name: Preparations
scenes.description: Tuesday and Wednesday by day. The party chooses a route and gathers what they need. Routes: down the waterway (fast, open), through the rows (slow, hidden, easy to get lost: Survival DC 12 per leg or lose a round), by the culvert under Fossum Lane (if found), or a decoy: Ward's Kenworth at the Fork bridge, Rolf driving a grain truck off it, the TV van's lights on the ridge road, Deputy Garnett's cruiser with its lightbar going at the far end of the field. Allies: Rolf (knows the field and every man in the line by voice), Deputy Garnett (badge, radio, a bowhunter's eye for corn at night), Pastor Tove (Steady Now; and she is an outsider who has eaten the bread since June; she is in as much danger as anyone), Xavier Boone (a .45 and a 16mm camera; he wants to film it, and should not, because the camera light is warm). Kit: kerchiefs wetted in the creek, not a bucket; flashlights with red cellophane, or none; dark clothes; Ingeborg's spare gumboots for Dawn; a bucket of creek water carried in a milk can (it was running water a minute ago: 2d6 to the Landlord, once, and drives it back 10 ft); the hose idea, which does not work in a cornfield, and the players should be allowed to discover that.
scenes.readAloud: From the rim of the Hollow, by daylight, you can see all of it: the stone house behind you in its lilacs; the corn in front, a gold sea nine feet tall, running north to the Fossum yard and its silos and east, three-quarters of a mile, to a line of willows where the creek is; the waterway, a green stripe of mown grass straight down the middle like a part in hair; Fossum Lane crossing it halfway, with a tractor parked on it already; and far off to the north the elevator, with its antenna, and the village, and the Fork bridge, and two grain trucks parked nose to nose across the bridge with a sawhorse in front of them. Somewhere down in the corn, a crow is calling. Behind you, the Cold Hole breathes out, white, and breathes in.

skillChecks.success: You walk the edge of the field by day and fix the route in your head: which rows lead where, where the culvert is under Fossum Lane, where the creek bank is low enough to get down. At night you will not get lost on the first leg, and you have found the culvert.
skillChecks.failure: Every row looks the same from the edge. At night it will be worse.

skillChecks.success: Everything you know agrees: it hunts by breath and warmth, it is barred by running water, and it cannot take Dawn before Harvest Days; tonight it can only hold her for the men to find. A wet kerchief, a face in the earth, a held breath, no light; and running water, carried or crossed. Nothing else will help: not salt, not iron, not a prayer, not a gun. (If an Occultist sets a wrong ward anyway, it does nothing, and the thing knows someone tried: on the first leg it comes to that character first.)
skillChecks.failure: There are a dozen folk remedies for things in the dark and you have no idea which, if any, apply here.

skillChecks.success: Deputy Garnett agrees to bring his cruiser to the far side of the creek on Wednesday night at eleven, lights off, at the low bank where the waterway meets the water, and wait. He has no authority in Hollow Fork once the town closes the roads. On the far bank, he has the whole county.
skillChecks.failure: Garnett says he will come if he can; the sheriff has him on patrol over the ridge Wednesday. He may be late.

encounters: None hostile by day. On Tuesday afternoon, two Fossum boys and Vernon Kittleson park their pickups at the Harvest Moon and sit in them, watching, all night, politely
If anyone tries the Fork bridge on Tuesday or Wednesday by day: two men in a pickup (Frightened Townsman stats) who apologise and will not move the trucks

acts.title: Wednesday Night: The Corn
acts.description: The pursuit-and-hiding night. Run it as four legs from the stone house to the creek, each a few minutes of game time and ten or fifteen minutes of table time. On each leg the party makes a group Stealth check (half or more must succeed) against the line's passive Perception (12; 14 if the party is carrying lit lights; 10 on a leg after a successful decoy). Failure: a pair of townsmen spots them, shouts on channel 14, and the party must fight free (the townsmen grapple and hold; Frightened Townsman stats), outrun them (Athletics DC 12 each, Dawn at disadvantage unless helped), or hide again. Three spottings in all and the line closes in around them. On legs 2 and 3 the Landlord comes through (see scenes): a fear check DC 15 for each character who sees it (DC 13 with Rule Three known; DC 17 in darkness with no light, which they will be), and each character makes a Stealth check DC 14 against it, with advantage if their breath is hidden (wet kerchief, face in the earth, or held), or it finds them (Frost Touch, and the Long Breath if three or more are together). If it finds Dawn, she is restrained by cold and the men find her in two rounds unless the party carries her. This is combat.json chases and fleeing on the scale of a field: running works, and the creek is the place the pursuer can't follow. The light goes out once tonight (dread.json light_and_dark): on leg 3, whatever lights the party carries die at once, all together, and stay dead until they cross the water.
objectives: Get Dawn from the stone house to the north branch of the creek, three-quarters of a mile, through the line and the corn
Hide from the thing in the rows; use what you know
Get across running water, all of you

scenes.name: The Line
scenes.description: Leg 1: from the stone house, through the windbreak and the rim path, into the corn. Ingeborg says 'She's asleep, Arnie,' on channel 14 at ten-twenty, and the party goes. At ten-thirty the line starts south from the Fossum yard: flashlight beams in the rows like a wall of fireflies, pairs every fifty yards, the CB crackling, the tractor's headlights on Fossum Lane, the dogs. The party is going east and south, across the line's front. Group Stealth vs passive Perception 12. The dogs: if a dog finds them (on any failed leg, 1 in 2), it bays and holds them at bay; Animal-wise characters (Farm-Raised's Up Before Dawn, Russ, Wes) can quiet it (WIS check DC 12), and Dawn's pocket of Ingeborg's rosettes will do it too. Nobody should hurt a dog. Leg 2: the rows, toward the waterway. Halfway down, the Landlord comes (next scene).
scenes.readAloud: You go into the corn and it closes behind you like water. In ten steps the stone house is gone, and the stars are a strip of sky between two walls of stalks, and every leaf you brush rasps like paper, so loud you are sure the whole county can hear. Somewhere to the north, a long way off and not long enough, a man's voice on a walkie-talkie says, "Ten-four, moving out," and then, all at once, there are lights: a line of flashlight beams strung out across the field from west to east, a quarter of a mile wide, flickering through the stalks, coming south. Each beam is a man. You can hear them now, the leaves rasping round them, and their voices low, calling to each other: "Ronnie? I'm here." "Keep the line, keep the line." A dog barks, and then another. You are in the corn, in the dark, and two dozen men are coming through it toward you, and every one of them has a red kerchief pulled up over his mouth.

skillChecks.success: The beams sweep past and you are not in them. You hear a man breathing hard through a wet kerchief ten feet away on the other side of a wall of stalks, saying 'Lord, Lord, Lord' under his breath, and then he is gone south and you are behind the line.
skillChecks.failure: A beam finds a face. 'Here! Here! Big Red, they're in the east rows!' Two men come crashing through the stalks, not swinging, reaching, saying 'Easy, easy, nobody's going to get hurt.' Fight free, run, or hide again.

skillChecks.success: You keep the rows straight and count them, and know exactly where the waterway is: forty rows east.
skillChecks.failure: You come out where you went in. A round lost; the line is closer.

skillChecks.success: You run, with Dawn's arm over your shoulders, through the rows, stalks whipping your face, and the shouting falls behind you. (Dawn has disadvantage on this check unless someone helps her; a Roughneck's Heavy Work lets them carry her at full speed.)
skillChecks.failure: You go down hard in a furrow. The beams swing toward the sound.

scenes.name: In the Rows
scenes.description: Leg 2 and leg 3. The Landlord comes up the waterway from the Hollow at about eleven and turns into the rows, a line of frost twenty feet wide moving through the corn at walking pace, toward breath. The line of townsmen, seeing the stalks go white, does what it always does: every man lies face down in the furrow with his wet kerchief over his mouth, and the line stops, and the radios go silent. The party has the field to themselves, with it. Each character: fear check DC 15 (13 with Rule Three known; darkness adds 2), and Stealth DC 14 against it, with advantage if their breath is hidden. Dawn needs someone to hold her kerchief and keep her face down. Anyone it finds takes Frost Touch; three or more together, the Long Breath. If it finds Dawn, the cold restrains her and the townsmen will find her in two rounds, unless she is carried. The guests' Shades come with it: voices in the rows, calling names: Dr. Gessler calling 'Russ? Russ, I'm over here, I've hurt my leg'; a young man's voice calling for his mother; Emmett Tilley calling, cheerfully, 'Is it time?' Anyone who follows a voice walks toward the frost. Leg 3: the light goes out. Whatever lights the party has die at once, all together, as the frost reaches them, and stay dead. Fire works (a Zippo, a flare, a kerosene bottle) and hurts it (vulnerable) and drives it back, and draws it straight back again to the warmth. Water from the creek, carried in a milk can, drives it back once. Ordinary weapons do half damage to a fog.
scenes.readAloud: It starts as a silence. The leaves stop rasping. The flashlight beams, all across the field, go out, or go down, one after another, as the men lie down in the furrows, and the radios go quiet. Then the cold reaches you: not a wind, a cold, flowing through the stalks at the height of your knees, and then your waist, and your breath smokes. Forty feet away, through the rows, the corn is turning white. A line of frost is moving through the field, stalk by stalk, leaf by leaf, feathering them silver in the starlight, at the pace of a man walking, coming this way. You cannot see anything in it. There is nothing in it to see. But as it comes, you hear it: a long, slow breath, drawn in, and in, and in, as if something enormous had put its face down to the ground to smell for you. And from somewhere in the white, a man's voice, pleasant, puzzled, calls a name. One of your names.

skillChecks.success: Face down in the furrow, the wet kerchief cold over your mouth, your cheek in the dirt, holding your breath as long as you can and then letting it out into the earth, slowly. The cold flows over your back like a river. Frost forms on your hair, your collar, your eyelashes. Something pauses above you, breathing in, and in, and goes on. It passed you by. (Advantage if your breath was hidden.)
skillChecks.failure: Your breath smokes up white into the starlight, and the frost line turns, and comes, and stops on you, and breathes in, and the warmth comes out of your mouth and your chest like a thread pulled from a sleeve. Frost Touch: 3d8 cold, CON save DC 14 or restrained by cold until the end of your next turn.

skillChecks.success: The voice calling your name is not your friend. It uses his words and his voice, and there is nobody in it; it is like a phonograph left playing in an empty house. Do not follow it. (Anyone who fails and follows a voice walks into the frost.)
skillChecks.failure: It sounds exactly like him. He sounds hurt.

skillChecks.success: Whoever the cold touched: hands white and numb, lips blue, but not frostbitten if you get them moving in the next minute. Rub, breathe into them, keep going; a Physician's Steady Hands works here as anywhere.
skillChecks.failure: Their hands won't close. They will need help over the last leg.

scenes.name: The Water
scenes.description: Leg 4: the last two hundred yards, from where the rows end through the willows and box elder to the north branch of the creek. Two men at the creek where the waterway meets it (Frightened Townsman stats), lying face down until the cold passes and then getting up with their flashlights. The Landlord, if it has not been driven back, follows the warmth toward the water and stops at the bank (Rule Two). Deputy Garnett's cruiser, if he came, is on the far side with its lights off, and switches them on. The water is knee-deep, fast and cold over gravel: wading it is Athletics DC 10 (Dawn at disadvantage unless helped; failure means going down in the water, wet and cold, not drowned). On the far bank, Dawn is out of the Landlord's land for good. The men on the near bank stop. They stand with their flashlights at the edge of the water. Arnie Fossum, if he is there, sits down on the bank and puts his face in his hands. Somebody calls across, without anger, 'You don't know what you've done.' And behind them, in the corn, the frost turns away from the water, and goes back down the waterway toward the Hollow, and the stalks it passed stay white. If the party fails, Dawn is caught, carried back gently, and taken to Dr. Kubicek's clinic, where she is kept 'resting' until Harvest Days; the party, unless they hurt someone, is walked back to the motel and the pickups sit outside it all night.
scenes.readAloud: The corn ends and there is a strip of willows, black against the stars, and the sound of water. You come through the willows sliding on mud and there it is: the creek, twelve feet of fast dark water chuckling over stones, and beyond it the far bank, and on the far bank, all at once, a pair of headlights and a red-and-blue lightbar flaring on, and a man's voice shouting your names. Behind you, in the corn, the frost is coming. You can hear it breathing. You go into the water. It is so cold it takes your breath away, knee-deep, pulling at your legs, the stones rolling under your boots, and you have someone's arm over your shoulder, and you are halfway, and the cold behind you reaches the bank, and stops. Just stops. As if it had come to the edge of the world. On the bank behind you, white mist hangs over the water's edge, and does not cross, and breathes in, once, long and slow, and you feel it pull at the warmth in your back, from the far side of the water, and fail.

skillChecks.success: Across, all of you, wet to the thighs, shaking, on the far bank in the headlights. Dawn is out. The Landlord cannot touch her while she stays out of its land. Every character present loses 1 Dread for the relief of it (not a creature laid to rest; just the far bank).
skillChecks.failure: You go down in the creek, all the way, and come up gasping and soaked, and someone drags you the rest of the way. You are across. You will not stop shaking for an hour.

skillChecks.success: Across the water, to the men on the far bank: whatever you say, Arnie Fossum hears it. He does not answer. But Rolf Haugen, if he is with you, calls each man by name, and one by one they turn off their flashlights and go home.
skillChecks.failure: The men stand on the bank with their lights on you until you are gone.

skillChecks.success: Looking back from the far bank: the line of white stalks the frost left through the field, curving from the waterway to wherever each of you lay down, and back. And standing at the top of the field, on the rim by the stone house, a small figure with a lantern: Ingeborg, watching. She lifts the lantern, once.
skillChecks.failure: Darkness, and the corn, and the cold.

encounters: Arnie Fossum's line: twenty-four townsmen (Frightened Townsman; Arnie and three others Night Watchman), in pairs, who grapple and hold and do not strike first; no guns. A party that shoots one of them has made a terrible thing worse, and the GM should let them feel it.
The Fossum dogs (Feral Dog stats), which bay and hold; quiet them, do not hurt them
The Landlord in the rows (campaign controlFile): fear check DC 15, Stealth DC 14 to be passed by, Frost Touch, the Long Breath; it cannot take Dawn tonight, only hold her
Shades of the guests (Shade stats), calling names; harmless unless followed into the frost

acts.title: Thursday: The New Name
acts.description: The morning after. Whether Dawn is over the water or back in the clinic, the town wakes up knowing that the strangers are at war with it. The phones go dead. The bridge stays closed. And the rent must be paid. The point of this act is the cost of success: if Dawn is out, someone else must be the guest, and Harald Haugen strikes her name and inks a player character's; and the party's first real conversation with the man who writes the names, who is ready to stop.
objectives: Get Dawn, if she is out, somewhere safe and out of the watershed, and get word to the outside
Learn whose name is now in the Book
Meet Harald Haugen and decide which door to try

scenes.name: The Phones Go Dead
scenes.description: Thursday 10 October, seven in the morning: the telephone exchange goes down (keyLocations). Dawn, if she is out, must go somewhere outside the watershed: Deputy Garnett can take her to the hospital in Linden Falls; Emil Pospisil's Friday bus; Einar's trailer in Winona, where there is a hose across the step. Tess will want to go with her and be needed here. In town, the party's motel rooms have been cleaned, their beds turned down, and a plate of bars left on each pillow with a note in Elsie's hand: 'Please come to the diner. We need to talk. E.' At the diner, Elsie, who has not slept, tells whoever comes that the board met at six this morning, and Harald wrote a new name, and she is so sorry, and would they like some breakfast. She brings it. She does not cry until she is in the kitchen.
scenes.readAloud: The diner is empty except for Elsie. The chairs are still up on the tables. She has made coffee anyway, and set out cups, and she sits down across from you in the big booth by the jukebox, where you sat the first day, and folds her hands on the Formica, and for a while she does not say anything at all. "They met at six," she says. "The board. In Harald's office. Arnie and Marit and Arlen and me and Harald, and Inga didn't come, she's never not come." She looks at the window. "He struck the girl. You have to strike a name with the same hand that wrote it, so he did. And then he wrote the other one in ink, the one he'd put in pencil, because the rent has to be paid, hon. It has to be. You don't know what happens when it isn't." She looks at one of you, and her eyes fill. "I'm so sorry. I'm so sorry. Would you like some breakfast? Let me get you some breakfast."

skillChecks.success: Elsie tells you: the name is (the alternate's). She tells you the board is split. Marit and Arnie want it paid. Dr. Kubicek says nothing and won't look at anyone. Harald wrote it and went home and didn't come in to work. And she, Elsie, doesn't know any more. 'Arvid says if we lose the luck we lose the luck. Arvid says he's had fifteen years he wasn't supposed to have and he'd give them back. I can't, hon. I can't lose him. But I can't do this again either.' (A crack in the house of Brandvold.)
skillChecks.failure: Elsie cannot say the name. She brings breakfast. She goes into the kitchen. Arvid comes out, sits down where she sat, and tells you whose it is.

skillChecks.success: At the exchange hut, with the Fossum boy distracted: the fuses back in, the test board patched, one long-distance call out over the trunk before someone notices. Quentin's editor, Tess's hospital, the State Patrol, the TV station: one of them.
skillChecks.failure: The fuses are gone, taken away. You will need the CB, the cruiser radio or the Friday bus.

skillChecks.success: Elsie is not a villain and never was. She is a woman who has been kind to seventy years of guests and has lived with it by not thinking. She is thinking now. She can be brought to the Cold Hole, if Arvid comes with her.
skillChecks.failure: Elsie is breaking, and you cannot tell which way.

scenes.name: The Hand That Writes
scenes.description: Thursday night, after midnight: Harald Haugen's office (keyLocations), or Harald on the motel step in his overcoat with the Book under his arm, if Rolf has told him where they are. He gives CLUE 4a to anyone who has not seen it, confirms the two doors, and says the surrender is the right one and that he does not believe the six houses will do it, 'because I wouldn't have, last year'. If the party asks him to speak for the house of Haugen at the Cold Hole, he says yes. Then: 'If they won't, there's the other door. It's my hand.' Play this straight and sad. He is a good man who has done a monstrous thing nineteen times for reasons he could explain to a judge, and he knows exactly what he is. Players may want to punish him; let them say anything they like; he agrees with all of it. Do not let a player push him toward the second door; if a player tries, he says, mildly, 'That's mine to decide, son,' and changes the subject. GM: if the paying out happens in hs-scenario-004, it must be his choice, made in the moment, and played with gravity.
scenes.readAloud: He looks older than he did at the Fall Supper; he looks older than he did on Monday. His tie is gone and his collar is open and there is a cut on his chin where he shaved badly. The Book is on the desk in front of him, open, and the fountain pen is beside it with its cap off, drying. "I struck her," he says. "Same hand. You have to. And I wrote your friend in, because six people told me to and because I've done it nineteen times and the twentieth is no harder. That's the thing nobody tells you. It doesn't get harder." He turns the Book round on the blotter so you can read it, and taps the first page with one finger: THE AGREEMENT OF 24TH AUGUST 1904, and seven names. "Two doors. You know them. The first one is everybody together. I'll go through it. I don't think the others will." He sits back. "And the second one has my name on it. It's had my name on it since 1955."

skillChecks.success: Harald is not threatening anything and not asking for anything. He is telling you the truth because nobody else will. He loves his son. He loves his town. He has hated himself since he was thirty-nine. He would choose the surrender over the other door, if the others would come, because the other door leaves Rolf alone.
skillChecks.failure: A tired man in an office at one in the morning. You cannot tell what he will do.

skillChecks.success: Harald will speak for the house of Haugen at the Cold Hole, and he will give the party the Book to carry there, and he will go to the board on Friday and tell them so. (Each house the party wins counts in hs-scenario-004.)
skillChecks.failure: Harald says he will speak for the Haugens if the others do. He has said that before, in his own head, every Labor Day.

skillChecks.success: The first page, read with care: 'surrendered by every house that set its name hereto, reading back its own line, at the place of agreement, at the last light of the harvest feast'. Not the heads of the houses. Every house. 'By blood or by marriage', it says, in Gunnar Haugen's copperplate, a careful man's careful clause. Any living member of a house can read its line. Lillian Fossum can speak for the Fossums. Sylvie Aldahl can speak for the Aldahls. Rolf for the Haugens. (This is the clue that makes the surrender possible without the hardest keepers.)
skillChecks.failure: The terms are in an old, formal hand. It says the houses must surrender it. You assume that means the heads.

scenes.name: Seven Houses
scenes.description: Thursday night or Friday morning: the plan. The party, with Harald or Rolf or Ingeborg, lists the seven houses and who could speak for each at the Cold Hole at last light on Saturday. This is the setup for hs-scenario-004; let the players work it out at the table. VAAGE: Ingeborg (willing). HAUGEN: Harald (willing, if the others are) or Rolf (willing). BRANDVOLD: Elsie (breaking; will come if Arvid comes) or Arvid (willing; he is a Brandvold by marriage, and it counts). KUBICEK: Dr. Arlen (unwilling; Gary) or Gary Kubicek, 26, the vet, the saved child, who does not know what saved him and must be told (the hardest conversation in the campaign). LUNDE: Marit (unwilling, the hardest keeper) or her son Kjell, 30, the bank's loan officer, who hates the bank and loves his mother. FOSSUM: Arnie (unwilling) or Lillian (by marriage; she has been praying for this). ALDAHL: Einar, across the river (afraid), or Sylvie Aldahl, a player character, by blood. Each needs a scene in hs-scenario-004. The party also has two problems: the name in the Book is now one of theirs (that character is the guest, and at last light the Landlord will call them; they must not be at the supper, or must be held), and the TV van comes at six on Saturday.
scenes.readAloud: Somebody finds a pencil, and Elsie's order pad, and writes it down in a column, the way you would plan a church supper or a barn raising: VAAGE. HAUGEN. BRANDVOLD. KUBICEK. LUNDE. FOSSUM. ALDAHL. Seven houses. Seven farmers who went down a path in the dark in 1904 with lanterns, and signed their names in a book, and made a town. Next to each, a name, or two, or a question mark. Next to KUBICEK, a question mark, and next to it someone has written LOWELL? and then crossed it out and written it again. Next to ALDAHL, two names, one of them across a river and one of them at this table. Outside, the grain dryers are roaring, and the elevator's red light is blinking on top, and it is a day and a half to Harvest Days.

skillChecks.success: From the Book, the co-op's member rolls and Ingeborg's memory, you have every living member of each house by blood or marriage, and their ages and where they live. Every house has at least one person who might say yes.
skillChecks.failure: You have the heads of the houses and not much else. Ingeborg or Rolf can fill in the rest by Friday.

skillChecks.success: You can see the shape of it: Ingeborg and Harald will come; Elsie will come if Arvid does; Lillian will come and it will break her marriage; Sylvie or Einar for the Aldahls; Kjell Lunde, maybe, against his mother; and the Kubiceks are the hardest, because the only one who could say yes is the one the bargain saved, and he has two little girls, and has to be told.
skillChecks.failure: Seven houses, and most of them would rather the stranger died. That is all you can see tonight.

skillChecks.success: The surrender is a rite, and like every rite in this place it works only because its rules say so: every house, at the place, at the last light, reading back its own line. Miss one house, and nothing happens, and it knows you tried. It will fight; it will speak to each reader in the voice of what it gave them. You will need people beside each reader.
skillChecks.failure: You know what the words are. You do not know what will happen when you say them.

encounters: None hostile. The town is Closed. Pickups at the motel, the bridge blocked, the phones down, and everyone exhaustingly polite

If Dawn was caught: she is at Dr. Kubicek's clinic, sedated and watched by two townsmen; getting her out before Saturday is a scene of its own (Stealth DC 14, or Dr. Kubicek's cooperation, which is the beginning of the house of Kubicek turning)

npcsInvolved.name: Ingeborg Vaage, 82
npcsInvolved.role: The last witness; the first speaker
npcsInvolved.description: In her kitchen, with rosettes and the truth; on the rim with a lantern on Wednesday night.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Seventy stones. She would like there to be no seventy-first.

npcsInvolved.name: Dawn Petrakis, 22
npcsInvolved.description: Clear-eyed for the first time in a month, frightened, funny when she can manage it, in a borrowed housecoat and Ingeborg's gumboots.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Home. Her sister. Never to eat bread again.

npcsInvolved.name: Arnie Fossum, 49
npcsInvolved.description: In a barn coat and a wet kerchief, with a walkie-talkie and no gun, in the corn at night.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Nobody hurt. The girl back. The town safe. In that order, he tells himself.

npcsInvolved.name: Harald Haugen, 58
npcsInvolved.role: The hand that writes the names
npcsInvolved.description: In his office after midnight with the Book, the pen and an unopened bottle.
npcsInvolved.motivation: He is finished. He wants the surrender. He knows the other door is his.

npcsInvolved.name: Elsie Brandvold, 61
npcsInvolved.description: Alone in the diner with the chairs still on the tables.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Arvid, and seventy years of guests she was kind to.

npcsInvolved.name: Arvid Brandvold, 67
npcsInvolved.description: Out of the kitchen for once, flour on his hands, sitting where his wife sat.
npcsInvolved.motivation: He has had fifteen years he was not supposed to have. He would give them back.

npcsInvolved.name: Rolf Haugen, 24
npcsInvolved.role: Companion; knows every man in the line by voice
npcsInvolved.description: Little Elevator, in the corn, calling men by name across the creek.
npcsInvolved.motivation: That his father never has to write again, one way or the other.

npcsInvolved.name: Deputy Wes Garnett, 32
npcsInvolved.role: Companion; waiting on the far bank
npcsInvolved.description: A cruiser with its lights off at the low bank of the creek at eleven at night.
npcsInvolved.motivation: He has no authority on the near bank, and the whole county on the far one.

npcsInvolved.name: Pastor Tove Hagstrom, 31
npcsInvolved.role: Companion; an outsider who has eaten the bread since June
npcsInvolved.description: In jeans and her father's barn coat, saying 'Look at me. Breathe' in the dark.
npcsInvolved.motivation: She came to serve these people. She is going to, though not the way they think.

npcsInvolved.name: Lillian Fossum, 46
npcsInvolved.role: Arnie's wife; a Fossum by marriage
npcsInvolved.description: At the yard, making sandwiches for the line, and praying.
npcsInvolved.motivation: She has been eligible every year for twenty-four years. She would like it to end.

rewards.money: No money changes hands. If Dawn is out, Tess and Ward between them owe Deputy Garnett a steak dinner; Emil Pospisil will not take a fare. The town leaves a plate of bars on every pillow. Anything broken in the night (a grain truck, a cruiser's paint, a stand of corn) the co-op will quietly pay for, because that is the kind of town it is.
items: Dawn, out of the watershed (or not)
The town's plan, and the town's voices, on tape if anyone had a recorder running on channel 14
Ingeborg's account of 1904, and her word that she will speak first
The Book, or Harald's promise to bring it to the Cold Hole
Elsie's order pad with seven houses written down the side
Polaroids or 16mm film of the frost line through the corn (Xavier Boone, if he was there; the camera light drew it, and he has a frostbitten hand to prove it)

twists: The name in ink is a player character's (by default Russ Thorsen; otherwise whoever has eaten most of the town's bread). That character is now the guest: at last light on Saturday, the Landlord will call them (Calling the Guest, campaign controlFile), and the town will be kind to them in a whole new way. If they leave the watershed, the rent goes unpaid; if they stay, they must be held, or be at the Cold Hole for the surrender, which is the most dangerous place for a guest to be.
If no player character has eaten the town's food (a careful party), the alternate is Pastor Tove Hagstrom, who has eaten it since June.

Gunnar Haugen's careful clause, 'by blood or by marriage', makes the surrender possible without Marit Lunde, Arnie Fossum or Dr. Kubicek, and turns it into the campaign's hardest set of conversations: Kjell Lunde against his mother, Lillian against her husband, Gary Kubicek told what saved him.
The townsmen lie face down in the corn when it comes, exactly as the party learned to. They have been doing it all their lives. Nobody ever told them why it works, and nobody ever asked.
dmTips: The night in the corn is the campaign's set piece. Run it in legs, fast, with the CB voices and the flashlight beams, and give the players real choices: waterway or rows, together or split, decoy or none, light or dark. Do not let it bog down in rolls; a leg is one group check and a consequence.

The townsmen do not want to hurt anyone and will not bring guns. If the players shoot, the townsmen scatter and the night becomes a tragedy; the GM should let the players feel the weight of that without ending the campaign. A wounded townsman can be carried over the water with Dawn, and Deputy Garnett will take him to Linden Falls too.

The Landlord cannot take Dawn tonight; it can only hold her for the men. Make sure the players understand this before the night, through Ingeborg or Old Lore, so that its menace is cold and capture, not death.

The light goes out once, on leg 3. All the party's lights die together, and darkness adds 2 to the fear checks. Fire still works, and hurts it, and draws it. Let a clever player use a Zippo or a flare to save someone and then have to run from what it brings.
If the party fails and Dawn is caught, nobody is hurt; she is in the clinic, and hs-scenario-004 includes getting her out. The campaign does not end on a failed night.
After the creek, give the players a moment. Every character present loses 1 Dread. Let Tess and Dawn have their scene on the far bank in the headlights. Then the morning, and the new name.
Harald's scene sets up the paying out. It must be his choice. Never prompt a player to volunteer for anything; the second door belongs to the hand that writes the names, and that hand is his.
Budget an hour for Ingeborg and the preparations, an hour and a half for the corn, and an hour for Thursday.
